subject: zoology
question_text: Distinguish between euryhaline and stenohaline animals.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.68, Star Questions Plus, SAQ 190). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Euryhaline
lines: Euryhaline animals are adapted to withstand
wide fluctuations of salinity.
They can live in water whose salt content
changes over a wide range.
steps.why: The whole distinction is the width of the salinity range an animal can bear, so the definition must carry the word wide; the two Greek beginnings, eury and steno, then do the rest of the work.
common_mistakes: Writing that euryhaline animals live only in the sea. They live across a WIDE range of salinity.
Leaving out the word salinity. The range being described is a range of salt content.
steps.memory_tip: Eury means wide, steno means narrow. Haline means salt. Wide-salt and narrow-salt.
steps.margin_note: One sentence with the word wide in it. Keep the examples for the next step.

steps.label: Euryhaline examples
lines: Ex: brackish water fishes such as salmon
and Hilsa.
They withstand fresh water during low tide
and saline water during high tide.
Migrating fishes move from the sea into
fresh water to breed. This is anadromous
migration.
steps.why: The examples are the proof of the definition, and the migration is included because a fish that swims from the sea into a river passes through the whole range of salinity in one journey.
common_mistakes: Naming the fishes without saying what range they cross.
Calling the movement from the sea into fresh water catadromous. It is ANADROMOUS migration.
steps.memory_tip: Anadromous: up the river from the sea to breed. Salmon and Hilsa both do it.
steps.margin_note: Name the fishes, then the tide line and the named migration.

steps.label: Stenohaline
lines: Stenohaline animals are unable to tolerate
fluctuations in salinity.
They can live only within a narrow range of
salt content.
steps.why: The second half is written in the same shape as the first with the one word changed from wide to narrow, which is what makes a distinguish answer read as a comparison.
common_mistakes: Writing that stenohaline animals live only in fresh water. They may be marine or freshwater; the point is the NARROW range.
Swapping the two terms. Steno is the narrow one.
steps.memory_tip: Steno is the same beginning as in stenosis, a narrowing. Narrow range of salt.
steps.margin_note: Mirror the euryhaline sentence with wide changed to narrow.

steps.label: Stenohaline examples

lines.text: Eury = wide range, Steno = narrow range

lines: Ex: marine fishes die when they are placed
in fresh water.
Ex: freshwater fishes die when they are
placed in sea water.
Each of them can live only in the salinity
it is adapted to.
steps.why: The stenohaline examples are stated as what happens when the animal is moved, because the narrow range shows itself only when the salinity is changed.
common_mistakes: Naming a fish species. The examples here are the two groups, marine and freshwater fishes.
Writing that stenohaline fishes can adjust slowly. They cannot tolerate the change.
steps.memory_tip: Move a stenohaline fish across the salinity line and it dies. That is the test.
steps.margin_note: Both directions of the test, one line each. The box states the whole distinction.

insider_note: This is a distinguish question, so write the two definitions in the same shape with only wide and narrow changed — the paired examples then carry the other two marks.
